HSR Pity Counter Audit: Is 1.6% Normal? [2026]
items.summary: Check your Honkai Star Rail pity counter against published odds: 0.6% base, 1.6% average, 90-warp cap and about $186 expected for a featured 5-star.
items.content:
Your Honkai Star Rail pity counter is normal unless it breaks one of three published rules. A 5-star character must land within 90 warps on the same counter, a lost 50/50 must be followed by a guaranteed featured character, and the long-run average sits at 1.6% per 5-star, built on a 0.6% base rate . Everything else, including 70 dry warps in a row, is the game working as written.

The Published Warp Rates: Base Rate vs Average Rate How the Honkai Star Rail Pity Counter Works Pity-Cost Table: Warps, Stellar Jade and Cash Step-by-Step Expected-Value Calculation The Cheapest Warp: Express Supply Pass Math Probability Floor: Odds of a 5-Star Before Soft Pity How to Audit Your Own Warp History in 5 Steps Four Worked Examples With Real Numbers Example 1: 300 warps, 4 five-stars Example 2: losing 4 of 14 coin flips Example 3: one $99.99 pack, nothing to show for it Example 4: chasing a character and a signature Light Cone Impossible Results That Signal a Counting Error Myths vs Facts About Warp Odds What a Fair Gacha Audit Can and Cannot Prove FAQ How many warps do I need to guarantee a featured 5-star character? Can I lose the 50/50 twice in a row? Does pity carry over into Version 4.7? How much real money is one guaranteed featured character? Is Honkai Star Rail rigged against me? Related Coverage The cost follows from those rules. One warp costs 160 Stellar Jade, so the worst case for one featured character is 180 warps, or 28,800 Jade. The expected case is about 94 warps, or 15,000 Jade. What that costs in real money depends on your region, platform and the current Oneiric Shard package table, so no cash figure is given here.

These rules apply to the live game as of November 10, 2026, with Version 4.6 running and Version 4.7 scheduled to launch on November 11. The structure matches the 90-pull cap and 0.6% rate breakdown already on file. The useful question for a player is narrower: does my own warp history sit inside the normal range, and what did it cost me?

HoYoverse publishes two numbers for every limited banner, and they get mixed up constantly. The base rate is the chance on a single warp before any pity effect applies. The average rate (called the consolidated rate) folds the pity ramp into one long-run figure, which is why it runs higher. Per the in-game Details rules transcribed by Gaming Route , the Character Event Warp lists a 0.6% base and a 1.6% average. The Light Cone Event Warp lists 0.8% and 1.87%.

Read the 1.6% figure as a long-run frequency, not a per-warp chance. Divide 1 by 0.016 and you get 62.5 warps per 5-star on average. Individual runs scatter widely around that average because the early warps run at the flat base rate and the pity ramp does the rest of the work.

HoYoverse does not publish the exact warp where the ramp begins. Community testing, repeated in several current guides, puts the start of soft pity near warp 74 for characters. Treat that number as an estimate, not a rule. The only hard numbers are the base rate, the average rate and the cap. The ramp itself gets a closer look in this breakdown of soft pity and hard pity math .

The Honkai Star Rail pity counter is the number of warps since your last 5-star on a given banner type. Character Event Warps share one counter, so pulling on two character banners at once adds to the same total. Light Cone Event Warps share a separate counter. Neither counter touches the Stellar Warp or the beginner Departure Warp. That separation matters when you audit a history, because mixing banner types in one tally produces numbers that look broken but are not.

The 50/50 guarantee carries over too. If you lose the flip and your next 5-star is a standard character, the following 5-star on the limited-character track is the featured unit. Progress moves into the next Character Event Warp, so the jump from Version 4.6 to Version 4.7 resets nothing. Pity does not vanish when a banner ends. It moves with you to the next banner of the same type.

HoYoLAB runs an official Warp Records tool that reportedly displays the previous 12 months of records across six warp categories. Use it, or the in-game history, to read your counter. Count from the last 5-star on that banner type, note whether the guarantee was active, and record whether each 5-star was the featured unit. Those three data points are all an audit needs.

Cash cost depends on which pack you buy, your region, your platform and tax, and no confirmed package table is available, so this guide gives no dollar figure per shard or per warp. Check the in-game store for the current Oneiric Shard packs. One Oneiric Shard converts to one Stellar Jade.

Prices are US list figures as commonly shown in top-up listings. Regional pricing, taxes and platform fees shift them, and the in-game store is the final word. The first purchase of each pack tier reportedly pays a double bonus (12,960 shards for the $99.99 pack), which lowers the one-time cost. It applies once per tier and resets periodically, so the table ignores it to stay conservative. The full ladder is covered in the guide to Oneiric Shard pack prices and cost per warp .

items.title: Genshin Impact 7.2 opens the way for the Cryo Archon and Star Rail 4.7 bets on Aha
items.summary: Genshin Impact 7.2 brings a new map and two Electro characters, Mitya and Valeri, and confirms Anastasia as the Cryo Archon in 7.3. Honkai Star Rail 4.7 adds Aha as the first playable Aeon, reruns and the fortuitous Eidolon.
items.content:
Version 7.2 of Genshin Impact, titled The Hour of Destruction, arrives with a new map and two Electro characters: Mitya and Valeri. Additionally, Anastasia is confirmed as the Cryo Archon for 7.3. Meanwhile, Honkai Star Rail is preparing 4.7 with Aha as the first playable Aeon, reruns of Silver Wolf Lv. 999, Acheron, and Jing Yuan, and the fortuitous Eidolon, a mechanic that updates the kits of older characters.

The Star Rail update expands the options for building Elation teams and offers veteran players a way to recover outdated characters. The fortuitous Eidolon works as a design adjustment that revisits old abilities and adapts them to the current state of the game. This mechanic is not limited to boosting stats: it modifies interactions between abilities and opens up new combinations with recent characters. The rerun system with Silver Wolf Lv. 999, Acheron, and Jing Yuan accompanies this revision and allows older accounts to compete again without relying solely on the units of the season.

While Genshin saves Anastasia for 7.3 like someone saving dessert, Star Rail already lets you play an Aeon and calls that balance. The fortuitous Eidolon sounds like an honorable rescue of old characters, though in practice it is the game saying that your team from two years ago needs a revision. Zenless Zone Zero rests and Petit Planet moves toward its launch, so it is worth keeping a close eye on this design adjustment: nostalgia also gets patched.

items.title: Petit Planet’s Gacha System Will Only be For Cosmetics
items.summary: Petit Planet's approach to monetization is more focused on consistent player experiences rather than aggressive gacha-pushing.
items.content:
HoYoVerse ’s bread and butter is, of course, gacha games. From its first big hit in Honkai Impact 3rd to the breakout success of Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, and Zenless Zone Zero, gacha is what brings home the bacon . The items distributed through these games’ gacha banners usually include characters, weapons, equipment, and other assorted elements that directly impact your experience with the game. If you want to play, you gotta be willing to roll the dice.

With the looming release of Petit Planet, HoYo’s new Animal Crossing-style life sim game, players have been curious as to how, exactly, the gacha element will factor into this particular style of game. It’d be pretty lousy, for example, if you had to keep rolling on banners just to see all of the game’s villagers and experience their stories.

The new life sim gacha game is launching ahead of several other titles this winter.

However, in a departure from its established formula, HoYo’s actually taking a slightly different approach to monetization in Petit Planet. There will still be a gacha system, of course, but the only items this gacha will dispense will be strictly cosmetic, with all of the actual gameplay stuff being readily accessible to everyone whether they’re willing to roll or not.

At the HoYoverse Media Tour 2026 in Seoul, South Korea, two representatives from the Petit Planet dev team, lead game designer Murphy and lead artist Yinli Huang, explained their philosophy to the surrounding press.

In an interview with gaming outlet Geek Culture , Murphy explained that, rather than paywalling access to the game’s content through gacha banners or direct purchases, the goal is to make all of the actual gameplay elements available to all players, with whatever paid elements there being strictly limited to extra cosmetic stuff like character outfits and furniture.

“All of Petit Planet’s core gameplay, including its life simulation and all content related to forming friendships and building stories with the Neighbours, is included for all free players,” Murphy said. “In terms of our monetisation model, we can confirm that it will only be associated with cosmetics, meaning things like furniture and clothes.”

The goal is to make all of the actual gameplay elements available to all players.

This is quite a departure from HoYo’s other major titles. I play Honkai: Star Rail, for example, and because I don’t have every single character and all of their optimal gacha-earned equipment , I’m basically locked out of the game’s hardest endgame game modes.

Wuthering Waves is one of the biggest Gachas on the planet, and they do far better than most at answering player complaints. Let's go over exactly how!

Petit Planet is slated to specifically be a cozy life sim game rather than a management life sim. Many games of this genre purport to be cozy, but because they demand such constant, consistent engagement from you, they kind of stop being cute little daily life simulators and start being second jobs. The dev team is hoping to use the game’s live-service model to offer consistent, interesting content to the players without directly stoking FOMO.

“As a live-service title, we will constantly add new content to the game, like festival events, which are inspired by real-world festivals, alongside the concept of seasons,” Murphy told Geek Culture. “Each season, players will be able to meet new Neighbours, alongside new clothes and furniture to unlock.”

The crux of this pursuit is an as-of-yet undetermined system that would allow players to properly experience and reap the benefits of seasons’ past even if they weren’t playing the game at the time. Again, Star Rail does regular time-limited events, and while they all offer limited-time currency rewards, the actual gameplay elements remain accessible long after their endpoints. Even so, Murphy wants these types of events in Petit Planet to be as low-pressure as possible so players are interested without feeling obligated.

“We always come back to the randomness in daily life, so there’s no growth curve in our game, we just want to provide more of those little surprises and small pleasures in life for players.”

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail Dev Explains Aha & Discusses Future Playable Aeons
items.summary: Aha might be just the start of what
items.content:
Honkai: Star Rail Dev Explains Aha & Discusses Future Playable Aeons From Screen Rant on November 9, 2026 | OpenCritic

Genshin Impact brought the world of HoYoverse games to a much larger audience than ever before, but Honkai: Star Rail was the game that proved the company's staying power. Several years later, Star Rail is still going strong, even after the launch of Zenless Zone Zero and the impending release of games like Petit Planet and Honkai: Nexus Anima .

At a HoYoverse press event in Seoul, ScreenRant sat down in a group interview with Honkai: Star Rail 's lead game designer Chengnan An to discuss the state of the game and future plans. Honkai: Star Rail 's introduction of the first playable Aeon, Aha, naturally came up in the conversation, and the developers offered some details about both Aha's development and the potential for future playable Aeons.

First, Chengnan An addressed the tricky subject of making an Aeon playable in combat without upsetting the balance. While power creep always tends to come into the conversation with ongoing live-service games, HoYoverse doesn't want to simply drop an Aeon into the mix and " overcome all the existing characters ." In Aha's case, focusing purely on destructive strength would also fail to " fit her personality as an Aeon of Elation ."

items.title: HoYoverse Korea Unveils Two New Titles at Media Conference
items.summary: HoYoverse Korea announced on November 9 that it showcased key content for two new upcoming titles, Honkai: Nexus Anima and Petit Planet, during a media conference.
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ⓒ HoYoverse Korea HoYoverse Korea announced on November 9 that it showcased key content for two new upcoming titles, Honkai: Nexus Anima and Petit Planet, during a media conference.

The first domestic hands-on offline demos for both games will take place at G-STAR 2026. HoYoverse will participate with a 100-booth presence at the event held at BEXCO in Busan from November 19 to 22. The venue will also host booth events for Zenless Zone Zero alongside stage programs for Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail.

Set for a global launch on December 4, Petit Planet is HoYoverse's first planet life simulation game. Players take on the role of a 'Stargazer' to cultivate their own planet, enjoying life content such as growing crops and decorating structures. The game also features interacting with neighbors, exploring the sea of stars, and communicating with other players.

As a new entry in the Honkai series, Honkai: Nexus Anima combines 'Anima' collection and raising with strategic combat. Designed as an Anima-raising adventure strategy game set in a world where humans and mysterious creatures called 'Anima' coexist, players can enjoy 'Nexus Battles' that utilize the unique traits of each Anima.

The media conference was attended by HoYoverse Korea Country Manager Huang Ran, HoYoverse Global Business CEO Seven, and Global PR Communications Lead Sam, among others. Country Manager Huang Ran detailed the key features of the two new titles to be presented at G-STAR, after which key representatives answered questions about the games during a Q&A session.
